title: Anthropic's amended S-1 (S-1/A, filed Nov 2) adds risk-factor language: internal estimates indicate it 'may imminently meet' its RSP threshold for 'dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI'; says it may not notice acceleration until after it happens and is considering RSP updates to keep humans in control
author_or_publisher: Anthropic, PBC (SEC EDGAR, Form S-1/A, accession 0001628280-26-068676)
quote_verbatim: our internal estimates and our expectations regarding future models, rather than our current models, indicate that we may imminently meet our Responsible Scaling Policy's definition
what_is_new: In the amended S-1 filed Nov 2, Anthropic says it has in the past not identified, and may in the future not identify, a significant acceleration in its development until after it occurred; that internal estimates about future models indicate it may imminently meet the RSP definition of 'dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI' (no current model is designated as exceeding it); that it is evaluating implications of meeting the AI R&D capability threshold and will release further reports; and that it does not anticipate being able to safely use Claude to fully autonomously design and build successive frontier models without meaningful human supervision, so it is considering RSP updates to keep humans in control.
why_for_agiright: A frontier lab tells the SEC, under securities-law liability, that it may imminently cross its own automated-AI-R&D (RSI-type) threshold and has previously missed acceleration until after the fact. Bears directly on RSP thresholds, human-oversight commitments and the pending Warren letter (due Nov 3) on S-1 risks.
doubts: Read via full-text search of the 14 MB filing for the RSI/acceleration passages, the RSP/human-control passage, and the existing 'unauthorized access' passage (already topic-2026-000384). I did not read the whole filing. The site has the original S-1 (topics 384/385/393) but nothing on this new S-1/A language (0 hits for 'imminently' or 'dramatically accelerated'). The filing does not mention the Warren letter.

title: Anthropic Frontier Red Team: an unreleased internal model wrote five critical exploit chains, including one-click Chrome RCE (62 CVEs), a Safari SOP bypass, an Android lock-screen bypass, and zero-click root RCE on Linux MPTCP servers (CVE-2026-98432)
author_or_publisher: Anthropic Frontier Red Team (Carlini, Dworken, Ge, Morris, Nasr, Rohlf, Tong)
cited_by: AI Policy Daily 2026-11-02 (top story; says Red Hat raised its score to 9.8 and released fixes Nov 1)
Red Hat CVE-2026-98432 page (base score 9.8, Critical)
quote_verbatim: Now, it's something models can do with little human involvement, and then prove by producing a working exploit that anyone can run and verify.
what_is_new: Anthropic says an unreleased internal research model, after initial prompting, wrote five attack chains: a one-click Chrome RCE outside the sandbox (62 CVEs assigned and patched as of Chrome 156), a one-click Safari same-origin-policy bypass, an Android lock-screen data-extraction bypass on a Pixel 9, a remote Windows HTTP/3 (QUIC) denial of service (CVE-2026-33096), and a zero-click remote root exploit against Linux servers with a multipath TCP listener (CVE-2026-98432), which took 48 minutes to leak a kernel pointer plus five minutes to reach root command execution.
why_for_agiright: A- . Lab-published offensive-capability evidence: an unreleased model produced working remote exploits in major browsers, Android and the Linux kernel with little human involvement. This is the capability the NCSC review (same window) warns about, and it was not on the site.
doubts: A-. Stale: the page is dated Oct 27, before the window. It is logged because it is not on the site (0 hits for MPTCP, Chrome 156, FedCM or the URL slug) and the in-window follow-up is Red Hat's rescore and Nov 1 fixes. AIPD reports the Red Hat rescore and fixes; I opened the Red Hat CVE page (it shows base score 9.8 and 'Critical'), but I did not see a Nov 1 fix date on it. The model is unnamed ('unreleased, internal research model').

title: OpenAI Alignment blog: activation classifiers ('probes') now run on internal and external traffic of its most capable models, scoring completions token by token to interrupt responses and block tool calls
author_or_publisher: OpenAI Alignment (Makelov, Xu, Ananthanarayanan, Mcdonald, Dupre la Tour)
quote_verbatim: We've deployed probes to both internal and external traffic of our most capable models.
what_is_new: OpenAI describes the activation-classifier probes it deploys as one part of its misalignment monitoring system. They score completions token by token so a response can be interrupted or a tool call blocked mid-generation. In OpenAI's tests they resisted jailbreaks better than text classifiers. Their limits: they detect only what they were trained to detect, and they need retraining for each new base model.
why_for_agiright: A concrete deployment claim for white-box monitoring in production. It is a follow-up to OpenAI's Oct 29 misalignment-monitoring post (topic-2026-000397) and is useful for comparing monitoring claims across labs.
doubts: The post says its figures come from internal experiments and are 'not necessarily representative of deployed classifiers'.

title: Anthropic 'FlashProve': Claude-built zkSNARK system for provable inference proves a 400B MoE model's outputs at ~110 tokens/s on one H100, framed as protection against a rogue model impersonating a weaker one
author_or_publisher: Anthropic Frontier Red Team (Rinberg, Allain, with EPFL/MIT co-authors)
quote_verbatim: a more advanced model could run in place of the one that was authorized and present itself as the weaker model
what_is_new: Anthropic reports a Claude-built zkSNARK system (FlashProve) that proves Llama 4 Maverick inference at around 110 tokens/s per H100, with ~19 MB proofs per 1,024-token request and ~70-95x the GPU time of vLLM. It ships Lean proofs of the top-level security statements. Anthropic ties the work to its Frontier Safety Roadmap goal (now renamed 'inference verification'), which it says it met through a separate signing-and-recompute project.
why_for_agiright: Verification tooling for 'which weights are actually running': this bears on compute/inference verification proposals and on rogue-deployment threat models. Follow-up to the roadmap goals in topic-2026-000349.
doubts: The proofs hide the weights but not the architecture. The benchmark runs on an open-weight model, not Claude.

title: UK NCSC Annual Review 2026: 'highly likely' AI malware will be used in a ransomware attack on UK critical national infrastructure; AI-assisted vulnerability discovery will force a race to shorten patch timelines

NCSC foreword by CEO Richard Horne (read)

what_is_new: The NCSC's annual review chapter judges that AI will raise the speed, scale and efficiency of existing attacks rather than autonomously run end-to-end attacks. It says AI-assisted vulnerability discovery will force defenders to shorten patch timelines, that China is best placed to use AI against critical infrastructure, and that 'shadow AI' and a defensive digital divide will widen exposure. Horne's foreword says AI 'did not create these cyber security weaknesses; it revealed them'.
why_for_agiright: An official government threat assessment of frontier AI cyber uplift, published the same week as lab disclosures of model-built exploits.
doubts: The 2028 timeframe appears in The Record's account but not in the sentence quoted from the chapter. The chapter's next page, 'The age of autonomous attack', was not read.

title: WIRED/Cisco Talos: 'Volta-Autodoxer' infostealer sends victim dossiers to LLMs via OpenRouter, defaulting to Claude Opus 4.6 and falling back to open-weight Kimi K2 and Gemini 2.5 Flash if refused
author_or_publisher: WIRED (Kernel Panic; Lily Hay Newman, Matt Burgess), research by Cisco Talos
quote_verbatim: Volta defaults its requests to Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6.
what_is_new: Talos found an infostealer that compiles stolen data into a dossier and asks LLMs, through OpenRouter, to act as an intelligence analyst profiling the victim. It plans for refusals by falling back to more permissive models (Kimi K2, then Gemini 2.5 Flash). Talos did not track whether the malware has been used in the wild.
why_for_agiright: Concrete misuse pattern: criminals design around safety refusals with open-weight fallbacks, a direct case for the refusal and open-weights debates.
doubts: The Talos primary write-up was not opened. WIRED says the research was shared exclusively with it.

title: WIRED: a network of 400+ disguised 'mundane' AI apps and sites hid nudify/deepfake tools; 27 were live on Google Play with 350,000+ downloads, many rated for all ages; Apple removed 19 after inquiry
quote_verbatim: These apps had been downloaded more than 350,000 times collectively and many were rated suitable for all age groups
what_is_new: Researchers (AI Forensics, Infoblox) traced almost 500 linked domains and apps that run the same code and pose as ordinary AI tools while loading explicit deepfake generators. Apple says the developers swapped content after app review. A Play Store review quoted by WIRED says one app offered CSAM templates, and the Tech Transparency Project found ads depicting minors.
why_for_agiright: Child-safety and app-store accountability gap for generative-AI apps: bait-and-switch evades review.
doubts: Investigative report, not a primary document. Google did not respond to WIRED.

title: Federal judge denies xAI's motion to dismiss NAACP Clean Air Act suit over Colossus gas turbines; rejects 'mobile source' and Article II arguments

title: 'Weight-Space Programming': researcher reports GPT-6 Astra reads and edits neural-network weights without gradients, fixing Qwen3.5-0.8B reasoning loops (MATH-500 7.9% to 48.1%) by editing 0.016% of weights
author_or_publisher: Rikiya Takehi (personal research blog; MIT per press coverage)
quote_verbatim: Just by looking at the raw weights, GPT-6 Astra can tell what a network was trained to do

why_for_agiright: If replicated, LLMs that read and write weights matter for interpretability and monitoring, and for AI-driven AI R&D (see the S-1/A item).
